sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle with a completed UChicago mathematics bachelor’s; no master’s is required. International
applicants are expressly accepted. GPA threshold: 3.0 overall, last 60 semester hours, or completed graduate
degree. Admission remains competitive. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Review research fit; prepare electronic transcripts, CV, two-page SOP and three recommenders. Faculty
contact is optional. All applicants automatically receive funding consideration. Request any available fee
exemption before paying. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Optional; department says a faculty endorsement can help. Strongest listed matches: Perlman, Polstra, Sridhar
in algebraic geometry/commutative algebra; Lee and Alvarez in cluster/representation-related geometry.
Verify capacity for 2027. [s1] [s11] [s15]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Apply electronically through Graduate School; no hard copies to mathematics or Graduate School. Central site
supports additional materials after initial submission. Receipt tracking and replacement rules need
confirmation in the current portal. [s1] [s4]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 portal exists but conflicts with standing mathematics deadline. Stipend is explicitly 2026-27; no 2027-28
increase established. [s1] [s2] [s5]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Conflict]
Department asks all materials by January 15 for fall and October 1 for spring to maximize admission chances;
late applications depend on vacancies. The 2027 program portal instead displays no deadline/no priority
deadline. Use January 15 as the prudent complete-file target and confirm this conflict. No summer intake. [s1]
[s2]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Department’s January 15 fall / October 1 spring target covers ALL application materials; no separate grace
period for letters or scores is published. English scores may be unofficial for application; official scores and final
official records are required after admission if applicable. [s1] [s3]

Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL iBT 4.5 with every subscore ≥4 (79 before January 2026), IELTS 6.5 with each ≥6,
Duolingo 120 with each ≥110, or PTE 59. Tests must be under two years old at application; superscores
accepted. Upload score copy initially; official scores after admission. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Yes: a degree from a recognized English-speaking country OR at least two years of coursework there meets the
published exemption; the United States is listed. Thus completed UChicago undergraduate study qualifies, and
two completed years may qualify before graduation. A generic English-medium letter alone is insufficient
outside the exemption criteria. [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; department encourages submission if it strengthens the application, but expressly gives full
consideration with or without scores. [s1] [s7]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
GRE Subject scores are not required. The public page does not classify them as recommended, ignored, or
prohibited. [s1]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload legible transcripts, with translations if needed. Central international instructions require each institution
where ≥15 semester hours were earned; department says transcripts generally. Unofficial copies suffice for
review. After admission, final official records must come directly from institutions; native-language documents
plus certified English translations where applicable, with issuing-institution certification (not notary copies). [s1]
[s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters, preferably mathematics or related-field professors who taught or supervised research and can
assess graduate potential. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate application for normal departmental funding. Graduate School fellowships require departmental
nomination after admission; whether the department requests additional references or essays for a nomination
is not publicly specified. [s1] [s8]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Entering recommender email addresses leads to a request to upload a letter, but the public instructions do not
establish the precise trigger relative to saving/submitting the application. The October 2026 waiver instructions
explicitly allow letters to arrive after application submission, while departmental complete-file deadlines still
matter. [s4] [s9]

Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Interfolio letters are accepted; instructions refer applicants to Interfolio. Whether an already submitted letter
can be replaced or reused across cycles is not established. [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published mathematics PhD GTA stipend effective August 16, 2026: $27,810 for nine months ($3,090/month at
0.50 FTE in central table), plus up to 15 credits of tuition each fall/spring, single health insurance and
college/department fees averaging $600/semester. Summer support usually exists but no guaranteed amount.
This is a 2026-27 rate, not a Fall 2027 offer. [s5] [s6]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Ordinarily five years; sixth year case by case, generally no seventh. Renewal requires assigned duties, GPA
≥3.0 and prescribed coursework/exam/dissertation milestones. Exact offer terms control. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants are considered for departmental support. Instructional GTAs must complete ITAP;
admission English exemption does not establish exemption from teaching requirements. English Language
Institute students cannot hold internally funded assistantships. [s1] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typical full GTA is 20 hours/week (0.50 FTE). Duties include instruction, tutoring, grading and problem sessions.
Scholarships do not cover international-student fees, books or ancillary costs. Central FAQ notes a 14%
withholding charge on the international health-insurance grant, billed in October and March; verify individual
tax treatment/offer. [s5] [s6] [s8] [s10]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Normal financial support is automatic with admission application; no additional application. For Graduate

School fellowships, departments nominate admitted students. Ask the director whether any internal
nomination materials are needed. [s1] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Capstone Doctoral Fellowship advertises five years at ≥$35,000 annually, combining $25,000 Graduate School
fellowship with a 0.25 FTE departmental assistantship and remaining tuition/fees/insurance; departmental
nomination, full-time campus attendance. International eligibility for this named award is not explicit. Other
departmental scholarships: Ainsworth (applied-math priority), renewable Hasell Palmer, and Henry C. Miller Jr.
(talented doctoral candidates). Summer scholarships/teaching/RA are usual, not guaranteed. [s5] [s8]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$80 international; $65 US citizen/permanent resident. Nonrefundable and paid for each application. F-1 status
does not create domestic-fee eligibility. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Standing exemptions include prior UA Graduate School enrollment and qualifying US military/veteran
documentation. Free Application Week 2026 deadline was October 9 at 5 p.m. Central, already expired as of
research date; no refunds. No published general international hardship entitlement found. [s4] [s9]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
1. Algebraic geometry / representation theory
Michael Perlman
Equivariant D-modules, local cohomology, determinantal/Schubert varieties and mixed Hodge structures. [s11]
[s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2024 · Equivariant D-modules on 2 × 2 × n hypermatrices
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
2. Algebraic geometry / commutative algebra
Thomas Polstra
F-singularities, test ideals, birational and local methods in commutative algebra. [s11] [s13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2024 · On the Equality of Test Ideals
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Prashanth Sridhar
Derived and homological methods in commutative algebra and algebraic geometry. [s11] [s14]

Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Serre duality for dg-algebras
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
3. Cluster algebras / representation-related geometry
Kyungyong Lee
Cluster algebras, scattering diagrams, positivity, quiver representations and algebraic combinatorics; current
KIAS research listing corroborates recent papers. [s11] [s15] [q16]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Broken lines and compatible pairs for rank 2 quantum cluster algebras
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.

University of Alabama - Tuscaloosa
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Portal deadline conflicts with department: do not wait beyond January 15 without written confirmation.
• 2026 Free Application Week has expired.
• Funding figures are nine-month 2026-27 rates; summer and Fall 2027 rates require an offer.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle with a completed UChicago mathematics bachelor’s; no master’s is required. International
applicants are expressly accepted. GPA threshold: 3.0 overall, last 60 semester hours, or completed graduate
degree. Admission remains competitive. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Review research fit; prepare electronic transcripts, CV, two-page SOP and three recommenders. Faculty
contact is optional. All applicants automatically receive funding consideration. Request any available fee
exemption before paying. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Optional; department says a faculty endorsement can help. Strongest listed matches: Perlman, Polstra, Sridhar
in algebraic geometry/commutative algebra; Lee and Alvarez in cluster/representation-related geometry.
Verify capacity for 2027. [s1] [s11] [s15]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Apply electronically through Graduate School; no hard copies to mathematics or Graduate School. Central site
supports additional materials after initial submission. Receipt tracking and replacement rules need
confirmation in the current portal. [s1] [s4]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 portal exists but conflicts with standing mathematics deadline. Stipend is explicitly 2026-27; no 2027-28
increase established. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Funding consideration [Conflict]
Department asks all materials by January 15 for fall and October 1 for spring to maximize admission chances;
late applications depend on vacancies. The 2027 program portal instead displays no deadline/no priority
deadline. Use January 15 as the prudent complete-file target and confirm this conflict. No summer intake. [s1]
[s2]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Department’s January 15 fall / October 1 spring target covers ALL application materials; no separate grace
period for letters or scores is published. English scores may be unofficial for application; official scores and final
official records are required after admission if applicable. [s1] [s3]

Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL iBT 4.5 with every subscore ≥4 (79 before January 2026), IELTS 6.5 with each ≥6,
Duolingo 120 with each ≥110, or PTE 59. Tests must be under two years old at application; superscores
accepted. Upload score copy initially; official scores after admission. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Yes: a degree from a recognized English-speaking country OR at least two years of coursework there meets the
published exemption; the United States is listed. Thus completed UChicago undergraduate study qualifies, and
two completed years may qualify before graduation. A generic English-medium letter alone is insufficient
outside the exemption criteria. [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; department encourages submission if it strengthens the application, but expressly gives full
consideration with or without scores. [s1] [s7]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
GRE Subject scores are not required. The public page does not classify them as recommended, ignored, or
prohibited. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload legible transcripts, with translations if needed. Central international instructions require each institution
where ≥15 semester hours were earned; department says transcripts generally. Unofficial copies suffice for
review. After admission, final official records must come directly from institutions; native-language documents
plus certified English translations where applicable, with issuing-institution certification (not notary copies). [s1]
[s3]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three letters, preferably mathematics or related-field professors who taught or supervised research and can
assess graduate potential. [s1]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate application for normal departmental funding. Graduate School fellowships require departmental
nomination after admission; whether the department requests additional references or essays for a nomination
is not publicly specified. [s1] [s8]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Entering recommender email addresses leads to a request to upload a letter, but the public instructions do not
establish the precise trigger relative to saving/submitting the application. The October 2026 waiver instructions
explicitly allow letters to arrive after application submission, while departmental complete-file deadlines still
matter. [s4] [s9]

Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
Not established by the cited public admissions materials. Confirm in the current application or with graduate
admissions before relying on a rule.
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Interfolio letters are accepted; instructions refer applicants to Interfolio. Whether an already submitted letter
can be replaced or reused across cycles is not established. [s4]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required CV/résumé covering education, scholarly activity and relevant employment. No public page/word
limit, font, file-size or upload-versus-link alternatives are specified. Submit electronically. [s1]
Statement of purpose; Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Required statement of purpose: describe academic and career goals and particular mathematical interests;
maximum two pages. No public word limit, font, margins or separate research-interest statement are specified.
Submit electronically. [s1]
Personal / background statement; Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary;
Publications list; Course-list document; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate application for normal departmental funding. Graduate School fellowships require departmental
nomination after admission; whether the department requests additional references or essays for a nomination
is not publicly specified. [s1] [s8]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published mathematics PhD GTA stipend effective August 16, 2026: $27,810 for nine months ($3,090/month at
0.50 FTE in central table), plus up to 15 credits of tuition each fall/spring, single health insurance and
college/department fees averaging $600/semester. Summer support usually exists but no guaranteed amount.
This is a 2026-27 rate, not a Fall 2027 offer. [s5] [s6]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Ordinarily five years; sixth year case by case, generally no seventh. Renewal requires assigned duties, GPA
≥3.0 and prescribed coursework/exam/dissertation milestones. Exact offer terms control. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants are considered for departmental support. Instructional GTAs must complete ITAP;
admission English exemption does not establish exemption from teaching requirements. English Language
Institute students cannot hold internally funded assistantships. [s1] [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Typical full GTA is 20 hours/week (0.50 FTE). Duties include instruction, tutoring, grading and problem sessions.
Scholarships do not cover international-student fees, books or ancillary costs. Central FAQ notes a 14%
withholding charge on the international health-insurance grant, billed in October and March; verify individual
tax treatment/offer. [s5] [s6] [s8] [s10]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Normal financial support is automatic with admission application; no additional application. For Graduate

School fellowships, departments nominate admitted students. Ask the director whether any internal
nomination materials are needed. [s1] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Capstone Doctoral Fellowship advertises five years at ≥$35,000 annually, combining $25,000 Graduate School
fellowship with a 0.25 FTE departmental assistantship and remaining tuition/fees/insurance; departmental
nomination, full-time campus attendance. International eligibility for this named award is not explicit. Other
departmental scholarships: Ainsworth (applied-math priority), renewable Hasell Palmer, and Henry C. Miller Jr.
(talented doctoral candidates). Summer scholarships/teaching/RA are usual, not guaranteed. [s5] [s8]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$80 international; $65 US citizen/permanent resident. Nonrefundable and paid for each application. F-1 status
does not create domestic-fee eligibility. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Standing exemptions include prior UA Graduate School enrollment and qualifying US military/veteran
documentation. Free Application Week 2026 deadline was October 9 at 5 p.m. Central, already expired as of
research date; no refunds. No published general international hardship entitlement found. [s4] [s9]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Department January 15/October 1 complete-file targets versus portal no deadline/no priority date. Department
asks transcripts broadly; central international page specifies ≥15 credits per institution. Use the more inclusive
record set and seek deadline confirmation. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm Fall 2027 complete-file deadline, offer/commitment date, letter invitation/receipt/replacement
mechanics, 2027-28 stipend, named-fellowship international eligibility and nomination extras. Recent faculty
paper evidence is provided below; supervision capacity remains unconfirmed. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s8] [s11]
